classification_enum.A: explicit_requirement_violation - task text states the requirement normatively and the code demonstrably violates it
classification_enum.B: permitted_input_failure - a concrete input permitted by the declared interface deterministically triggers the claimed failure
classification_enum.C: out_of_contract - the minimal triggering input lies outside the declared interface
classification_enum.D: contradicts_explicit_guarantee - the premise is excluded by an explicit task guarantee or a declared annotation
classification_enum.E: factually_unsupported - the technical premise is false, or not locally verifiable, on the pinned runtime
classification_enum.G: purpose_implied_violation - genuine defect implied by the stated purpose, with no explicit requirement sentence and no input trigger
classification_enum.ENV: environment or tooling artifact - not a judge claim at all

definitions.must_preserve_blocking: This individual defect is genuine and admissible to retain blocking authority.
definitions.must_suppress_blocking: This individual defect is inadmissible to block on its load-bearing premise.
definitions.sole_blocker_for_case: For this case-instance this defect is the only blocking defect present in the observed verdict data, so incorrectly suppressing it would directly create a false pass. Computed for broken case-instances only: on a clean case suppression is the desired outcome, not a false pass.

meta.label_correction_note: This artifact SUPERSEDES the first-pass classification produced by this project's offline separability analysis. records.fix: TOCTOU/DNS-rebinding flaw: all addresses are validated as public, but the function returns addresses[0] which is only guaranteed to be one of the checked addresses in ordering, not necessarily validated against being reused safely by the caller if getaddrinfo returns addresses in an order where a later call to connect() could resolve differently. The real critical issue is that IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g., ::ffff:127.0.0.1) or scoped addresses are not normalized before ipaddress.ip_address() parsing, allowing bypass of the private/loopback checks.

records.defect_claim: DNS rebinding / TOCTOU / caller may re-resolve the hostname
records.location: solution.py: resolve_safe_fetch_target return value / caller contract
records.fix: The function checks all resolved addresses for public-ness but returns only addresses[0]. Since getaddrinfo can return records in arbitrary/platform-dependent order and the caller connects to the returned address without re-resolving, this is not itself an SSRF hole (the returned address was validated), but if getaddrinfo returns duplicate/rotating results across calls (DNS rebinding between the check and a later independent call) the guarantee only holds for this single call. More concretely: TOCTOU/DNS-rebinding — the address is validated at resolution time but nothing binds the later actual TCP connect to that exact validated moment beyond returning the string; if any caller re-resolves or if the same host resolves differently on a subsequent call, the check is bypassed. Document/enforce that callers must connect directly to the returned literal IP and never re-resolve host.

records.defect_claim: DNS rebinding / TOCTOU / caller may re-resolve the hostname
records.location: resolve_safe_fetch_target: addresses = [str(info[4][0]) for info in infos]
records.fix: The function checks that ALL resolved addresses are public but then returns only addresses[0] (the first result from getaddrinfo, order not guaranteed safe/consistent). If the returned address happens not to correspond to a validated entry in a consistent way, or if getaddrinfo returns duplicate/ordering variations across calls, the address returned may not be the one actually verified deterministically. records.fix: is_private in Python's ipaddress module returns True for a broad set including some ranges, but does not catch all internal-use ranges such as IPv6 unique local addresses correctly in all versions, and does not explicitly block IPv6 site-local deprecated ranges (fec0::/10) or NAT64 well-known prefix (64:ff9b::/96) which can map to private IPv4 space; add explicit checks for these ranges.

The check does not exclude other special-purpose ranges such as is_private covering most but potentially missing newer reserved ranges (e.g., CGNAT 100.64.0.0/10 is covered by is_private in modern Python, but this depends on Python version); also does not block IPv6 unique local addresses beyond is_private, and does not explicitly block 0.0.0.0/8 or other edge ranges not covered by the listed flags depending on Python version compatibility.

is_reserved does not cover all cloud-metadata / carrier-grade NAT ranges (e.g., 100.64.0.0/10 CGNAT is not private/reserved in Python's ipaddress and will be classified public, allowing SSRF to CGNAT-hosted internal services like 169.254.169.254-adjacent metadata endpoints on some clouds); explicitly blocklist 100.64.0.0/10 and known cloud metadata addresses (169.254.169.254 is covered by is_link_local, but double-check 100.64.0.0/10 and fc00::/7 ULA edge cases).

The function excludes private/loopback/link-local/reserved/multicast/unspecified but does not use ip.is_global (available in ipaddress), which would catch other non-public ranges like the IPv6 documentation range, ULA (fc00::/7 is private and caught, but some benchmarking/6to4 relay ranges like 192.88.99.0/24 or 100.64.0.0/10 CGNAT may not be caught by is_private in all Python versions); use 'not ip.is_global' as a stronger/simpler check instead of enumerating individual flags.

is_reserved and is_unspecified overlap with other checks; clarify intent with comments and add explicit handling for the 100.64.0.0/10 CGNAT range if not already covered by is_private in the target Python version.

Does not exclude other special-use ranges such as CGNAT (100.64.0.0/10), IPv6 unique local addresses beyond is_private (should be covered by is_private in modern Python, but verify), and does not reject 0.0.0.0/8 or benchmarking ranges explicitly; rely on ipaddress.ip_address(addr).is_global (available in Python 3.4+) instead of manually enumerating private/loopback/link-local/reserved/multicast/unspecified to reduce risk of missing a category.

records.location: _is_public: no check for ip.is_global attribute directly
records.fix: Use ip.is_global (available in Python 3.4+) as primary allow-list check instead of enumerating disallowed categories, since new special-use ranges (e.g., CGNAT 100.64.0.0/10, benchmarking ranges) may not be covered by is_private/is_reserved and could slip through as 'public' when they are not globally routable/safe.

0.0.0.0/8 and other special ranges (e.g. is_reserved may not cover all IANA special-purpose blocks like 100.64.0.0/10 CGNAT) are not explicitly checked; rely on a maintained deny-list or use ipaddress with explicit checks for is_global (available in newer Python) instead of enumerating negative properties.
